claude.sample_unit: evaluators (12 linguists, 16 clinicians, 14 family caregivers) rating 20 discharge instruction texts translated into 6 languages

links.outcome: Translation quality ratings of ChatGPT-4o alone vs professional linguist post-edited (human-in-the-loop) output
links.effect: Human-in-the-loop translations were comparable or better than professional translations in all languages (Armenian overall quality 3.9 vs 3.6, p=0.01), whereas ChatGPT-4o alone was poorest for Armenian (2.4) and Somali.
links.quote: For example, the mean overall domain rating for Armenian human-in-the-loop translations was 3.9 (3.7–4.2) for human-in-the-loop and 3.6 (3.4–3.9) for professional translations, a difference of 0.3 (0.1–0.5) ( p = 0.01).

links.outcome: ChatGPT-4o translation quality ratings across six languages relative to professional translation
links.effect: ChatGPT-4o rated poorest for Armenian and Somali (Armenian overall quality 2.4 vs professional 3.6, p<0.001); lower for Chinese and Arabic; comparable for Bengali and Spanish.
links.quote: Relative to professional translations, evaluators rated all domains for ChatGPT-4o most poorly for Armenian and Somali.

links.outcome: Preference and quality of AI-only vs human-in-the-loop vs professional translation, and time to completion
links.effect: Human-in-the-loop most preferred (46.5% vs 28.4% professional) and faster (7.1 vs 16.8 min, p<0.001); ChatGPT-4o least preferred in most languages.
links.quote: Across all languages, the mean time required to produce each translation was significantly faster for human-in-the-loop than professional translations (7.1 [95% CI 5.4–8.8] vs 16.8 [13.7–19.9] min, p < 0.001).

openai.sample_unit: pediatric discharge instruction source texts rated by 42 evaluators

links.effect: HITL Armenian overall 3.9 [3.7-4.2] vs professional 3.6 [3.4-3.9], p=0.01; preferred 46.5% vs 28.4%; time 7.1 vs 16.8 min.
links.quote: Conversely, human-in-the-loop translations achieved comparable, often better, outcomes to professional translations for all languages, (e.g., Armenian mean overall quality: 3.9 [95% CI 3.7-4.2] vs. professional 3.6 [3.4-3.9], p = 0.01), were most frequently preferred (46.5% vs. 28.4%) and had shorter mean translation time (7.1 [5.4-8.8] vs. 16.8 [13.7-19.9] min, p < 0.001).

links.effect: Armenian overall quality 2.4 (95% CI 2.1–2.7) vs professional 3.6 (3.4–3.9), p<0.001.
links.quote: Relative to professional translations, evaluators rated all domains for ChatGPT-4o most poorly for Armenian and Somali.

links.effect: Poorest ratings for digitally underrepresented Armenian/Somali; Armenian 1.2 (1–1.4) lower overall quality than professional, p<0.001.
links.quote: ChatGPT-4o exhibited variable performance relative to professional translations, with poorest ratings for digitally underrepresented languages (Armenian and Somali).

links.effect: Armenian overall quality was 2.4 (95% CI 2.1–2.7), 1.2 (1–1.4) lower than professional 3.6 (3.4–3.9), p<0.001.
links.quote: For example, ChatGPT-4o translations for Armenian received a mean rating for the overall quality domain of 2.4 (95% CI 2.1–2.7), which was 1.2 (1–1.4) lower than professional translations ratings of 3.6 (3.4–3.9) ( p < 0.001).

unlisted_practices: Professional linguist post-editing of AI-generated translations of patient discharge instructions before patient or family use.

links.effect: ChatGPT-4o Armenian overall quality was 2.4 (95% CI 2.1-2.7) vs professional 3.6 (3.4-3.9, p < 0.001) and was lowest for Armenian and Somali, but comparable for Bengali (3.6 vs 3.5, p = 0.15).
links.quote: Relative to professional translations, evaluators rated all domains for ChatGPT-4o most poorly for Armenian and Somali.

links.outcome: evaluator preference for standalone AI versus professional translation
links.effect: ChatGPT-4o was least preferred for 5 of 6 languages: Arabic (17.1%), Armenian (5.0%), Bengali (22.1%), simplified Chinese (13.6%), and Somali (14.2%).
links.quote: Except for Spanish, evaluators least preferred ChatGPT-4o translations for all languages, including Arabic (17.1% [10.9–23.3%]), Armenian (5.0% [1.1–8.9%]), Bengali (22.1% [15.2–28.9%]), simplified Chinese (13.6% [7.9–19.2%]), and Somali (14.2% [7.9–20.4%]).
